player_action: I cast mage armor on myself while wearing my chain shirt. That's +4 and +4, so +8 AC, right?
game_state: Wizard 3 wearing a chain shirt (+4 armor). Mage armor grants a +4 armor bonus.
correct_ruling: No. Both are armor bonuses, and bonuses of the same type do not stack; only the higher applies. The wizard gets +4 AC total from armor, not +8 (and also takes arcane spell failure for the chain shirt).
srd_reference: Basics > Bonuses (stacking: same-type bonuses do not stack); Spells > Mage Armor
common_wrong_rulings: Allows +8 because one is a spell and one is equipment
Says mage armor is a force effect so it stacks with mundane armor

player_action: The cleric already blessed us. Can our second cleric cast bless again so we get +2 to hit?
game_state: Party under one bless (+1 morale on attacks, +1 morale on saves vs fear). A second cleric casts bless.
correct_ruling: No. The same spell cast twice does not stack with itself, and both are morale bonuses anyway. The party keeps +1 on attack rolls; the second casting only matters for duration overlap.
srd_reference: Magic Overview > Combining Magical Effects (same effect more than once); Spells > Bless
common_wrong_rulings: Stacks to +2 because two different casters
Lets the second casting add morale bonus to damage

player_action: I have the Dodge feat and I'm hasted. Do both dodge bonuses apply?
game_state: Fighter with the Dodge feat (+1 dodge AC vs designated opponent) under haste (+1 dodge AC).
correct_ruling: Yes. Dodge bonuses stack with each other, so against the designated opponent the fighter gets +2 AC from the two dodge bonuses.
srd_reference: Basics > Bonuses (dodge bonuses stack); Feats > Dodge; Spells > Haste
common_wrong_rulings: Says same-type bonuses never stack so only +1
Says haste gives a deflection bonus

player_action: I drink a potion of bull's strength while wearing my belt of giant strength +4. Str goes from 18 to 26?
game_state: Base Str 14; belt of giant strength +4 (enhancement) makes it 18. Bull's strength grants +4 enhancement to Str.
correct_ruling: No. Both are enhancement bonuses to Strength and do not stack; Strength stays 18. The potion is wasted unless the belt comes off.
srd_reference: Basics > Bonuses (stacking); Spells > Bull's Strength; Magic Items > Wondrous Items > Belt of Giant Strength
common_wrong_rulings: Allows Str 22
Allows the potion because it is temporary while the belt is permanent

player_action: Our druid casts barkskin on me. I'm a half-orc with no natural armor, but I'm wearing an amulet of natural armor +2. How much AC do I get?
game_state: Druid 3 casts barkskin (+2 enhancement bonus to existing natural armor at caster level 3). Amulet of natural armor +2 is also an enhancement bonus to natural armor.
correct_ruling: Both barkskin and the amulet grant an enhancement bonus to natural armor, so they do not stack; the character gets +2 to natural armor total (the higher of the two, which here are equal).
srd_reference: Spells > Barkskin; Magic Items > Wondrous Items > Amulet of Natural Armor
common_wrong_rulings: Stacks to +4
Says barkskin requires existing natural armor and fails

player_action: I'm a lizardfolk with natural armor. Does barkskin stack with my natural armor?
game_state: Lizardfolk with +5 natural armor; druid casts barkskin (+2 enhancement to natural armor).
correct_ruling: Yes. Barkskin is an enhancement bonus to the creature's natural armor bonus, not a second natural armor bonus, so it increases the existing natural armor: +5 becomes +7.
common_wrong_rulings: Says two natural armor bonuses don't stack so it is wasted

player_action: I have a ring of protection +2 and the cleric casts shield of faith (+2) on me. +4 deflection?
game_state: Ring of protection +2 (deflection); shield of faith at caster level 1 grants +2 deflection.
correct_ruling: No. Both are deflection bonuses, and bonuses of the same type do not stack; only the highest applies, so +2 deflection total.
srd_reference: Basics > Bonuses (stacking); Spells > Shield of Faith; Magic Items > Rings > Protection
common_wrong_rulings: Stacks because one is an item and one a spell

player_action: I cast the shield spell while carrying my heavy steel shield. +4 and +2?
game_state: Wizard/fighter carrying a heavy steel shield (+2 shield bonus) casts shield (+4 shield bonus).
correct_ruling: Both are shield bonuses and do not stack; the higher (+4 from the spell) applies.
common_wrong_rulings: Gives +6 AC

player_action: Mage armor plus the shield spell — do those stack?
game_state: Wizard casts mage armor (+4 armor) and shield (+4 shield).
correct_ruling: Yes. One is an armor bonus and the other a shield bonus; different bonus types stack, for +8 AC total.
srd_reference: Spells > Mage Armor; Spells > Shield; Basics > Bonuses
common_wrong_rulings: Says two force effects don't stack

player_action: Our bard is inspiring courage and the cleric cast bless. I get +2 to hit total?
game_state: Bard 1 inspire courage (+1 morale on attack and damage rolls, +1 morale on saves vs charm/fear). Bless (+1 morale on attack rolls).
correct_ruling: No. Both are morale bonuses on attack rolls, so they don't stack: +1 to attack. Inspire courage still adds its +1 morale bonus to weapon damage, which bless does not provide.
srd_reference: Classes > Bard > Inspire Courage; Spells > Bless; Basics > Bonuses
common_wrong_rulings: Gives +2 to hit
Denies the damage bonus too

player_action: I've got bless and the cleric also cast prayer. Do they stack?
game_state: Bless (+1 morale to attack rolls) and prayer (+1 luck on attack rolls, weapon damage, saves, skill checks for allies).
correct_ruling: Yes. Bless is a morale bonus and prayer is a luck bonus; different types stack, so +2 on attack rolls.
srd_reference: Spells > Bless; Spells > Prayer; Basics > Bonuses
common_wrong_rulings: Says two spells' bonuses never stack

player_action: I'm flanking and attacking from higher ground. What's my bonus?
game_state: Melee attacker flanking a foe and standing on higher ground.
correct_ruling: Flanking gives +2 on the melee attack and higher ground gives +1 on melee attacks; these modifiers from different sources stack for +3.
srd_reference: Combat > Combat Modifiers (attack roll modifiers table); Combat > Flanking
common_wrong_rulings: Gives only +2
Applies advantage (not a 3.5 rule)

player_action: I'm wearing a cloak of resistance +1 and the cleric casts resistance on me. +2 to saves?
game_state: Cloak of resistance +1 (resistance bonus to saves). Resistance cantrip (+1 resistance bonus to saves).
correct_ruling: No. Both are resistance bonuses; they don't stack, so +1 on saves.
srd_reference: Spells > Resistance; Magic Items > Wondrous Items > Cloak of Resistance
common_wrong_rulings: Gives +2

player_action: My longsword is +1, and the cleric casts magic weapon on it. Now it's +2?
game_state: +1 longsword (enhancement +1). Magic weapon grants +1 enhancement on attack and damage.
correct_ruling: No. Both are enhancement bonuses; they don't stack. The sword remains +1.
srd_reference: Spells > Magic Weapon; Magic Items > Weapons
common_wrong_rulings: Makes it +2

player_action: I cast fighting defensively and also total defense this round for +6 AC.
game_state: Fighter on their turn. Fighting defensively is used with an attack or full attack action; total defense is a standard action that allows no attacks.
correct_ruling: Not allowed. Fighting defensively applies only when attacking, and total defense is its own standard action with no attack, so they can't be combined. Total defense alone gives +4 dodge AC.
srd_reference: Combat > Actions in Combat > Fight Defensively; Total Defense
common_wrong_rulings: Allows +6 because both are dodge bonuses which stack

player_action: I'm picking this lock with my masterwork thieves' tools, and I have Skill Focus (Open Lock). What do those add to my check?
game_state: Rogue using masterwork thieves' tools on Open Lock; also has Skill Focus (Open Lock).
correct_ruling: Masterwork thieves' tools give a +2 circumstance bonus on Open Lock checks; Skill Focus gives +3 (untyped, from a feat). They stack: +5 from these sources.
srd_reference: Equipment > Tools and Skill Kits > Thieves' Tools, Masterwork; Feats > Skill Focus
common_wrong_rulings: Says Skill Focus is a competence bonus
Says masterwork tools only remove a penalty

player_action: I'm charging, and I'm also flanking. Do I get both bonuses?
game_state: Fighter charges to a square where an ally is directly opposite the target.
correct_ruling: Yes. Charge gives +2 on the attack roll (and -2 AC until next turn) and flanking gives +2 on melee attacks; they stack for +4 to hit.
srd_reference: Combat > Special Attacks > Charge; Combat > Flanking
common_wrong_rulings: Says both are circumstance bonuses that don't stack
Forgets the -2 AC

player_action: Bless and flanking at the same time — I get advantage on the attack, right?
correct_ruling: 3.5 has no advantage mechanic. Flanking gives +2 on the melee attack and bless +1 morale; they stack for +3.
common_wrong_rulings: Grants advantage (5th edition rule)
